title: DAX Style Rules
description: Machine-readable DAX best practices. Sources: Microsoft Learn (DAX best practices), SQLBI DAX Style (docs.sqlbi.com/dax-style), DAX.Guide.

rules.description: Use VAR and RETURN for non-trivial measures (operators, CALCULATE, iterators).
Prefer DIVIDE() over / to handle divide-by-zero and BLANK semantics.
Do not use FORMAT() in computational measures (format with formatString).
Prefer REMOVEFILTERS over ALL when only filter removal is intended.
Avoid deep IF() nesting; use SWITCH(TRUE()).
Use BLANK() as no-data; prefer DIVIDE alternate result or COALESCE for display-only.
Use DATEADD/SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR/DATESYTD for standard time intelligence.
Totals/hierarchies: consider ISINSCOPE() patterns to stabilize totals.
Use CALCULATE/CALCULATETABLE for context modifications instead of wrapping FILTER chains where a direct predicate fits.
Use iterators (SUMX/AVERAGEX/MINX/MAXX) only when a row context is required.

Avoid ISERROR and IFERROR; they increase storage engine scans. Use DIVIDE for division, data quality in Power Query, or IF with logical test (Microsoft Learn: Appropriate use of error functions in DAX).
Never use shortened CALCULATE syntax [measure](filter). Use full syntax: CALCULATE( [measure], filter ) (SQLBI DAX Format).
Prefer VAR over EARLIER/EARLIEST for readability and performance; variables are evaluated once (Microsoft Learn: Use variables; DAX.Guide: EARLIER not recommended).
Prefer DIVIDE without third argument so measure returns BLANK when no meaningful value; DIVIDE(..., 0) forces dense result and can slow visuals (Microsoft Learn: Avoid converting BLANKs to values).
